interpretations: Count all Laboratory records whose ID matches a Patient (inner join on ID), grouped by Patient.SEX. Return sexes whose count is above the average count per sex. Show sex, count, share of the total (count divided by the total matched records), and the difference between count and the average, unrounded.
Same as above, but "average per sex" is the mean of per-sex record counts across only the sexes that appear in the matched data (excluding NULL or empty SEX groups).
Same as above, but a NULL or empty SEX is treated as its own group, and it is included when computing the average and in the output.
Same as above, but "average per sex" is the total number of matched records divided by the number of distinct sexes in the Patient table (including sexes with no lab records).
Same as above, but "average per sex" is the average number of records per patient within each sex (records ÷ patients of that sex), and the comparison is on this per-patient rate.
"Share of the total" is the sex's count as a fraction (0–1) of all matched lab records.
"Share of the total" is the sex's count as a percentage (0–100) of all matched lab records.
"Share of the total" is computed against all Laboratory records, including those with no matching patient.
"How far above the average" is the absolute difference (count − average).
"How far above the average" is the relative difference ((count − average) ÷ average), as a fraction.
"How far above the average" is the relative difference expressed as a percentage.
"Test records" are counted as the number of Laboratory rows (each ID/Date pair).
"Test records" are counted as distinct test dates per sex.
"Test records" include Examination records instead of Laboratory records (the Examination table also holds test results).
"Test records" are Laboratory rows plus Examination rows combined per sex.
"Test records" are counted as the number of distinct patients with at least one lab record, per sex.
"Unrounded" means that no rounding or formatting is applied to the average, share, or difference values (raw floating-point or exact decimals).
"Unrounded" applies only to the "how far above" value, while the share may be rounded.

queries:
WITH counts AS (
    SELECT P.SEX AS SEX, COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM Laboratory L
    INNER JOIN Patient P ON L.ID = P.ID
    GROUP BY P.SEX
),
stats AS (
    SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_cnt, SUM(cnt) AS total_cnt
    FROM counts
)
SELECT c.SEX,
       c.cnt AS count,
       c.cnt * 1.0 / s.total_cnt AS share,
       c.cnt - s.avg_cnt AS diff_from_avg
FROM counts c, stats s
WHERE c.cnt > s.avg_cnt;
SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Patient WHERE SEX IS NOT NULL AND SEX <> '' GROUP BY SEX);
SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(SEX, ''), 'Unknown') AS SEX, AVG(strftime('%Y', 'now') - strftime('%Y', Birthday)) AS avg_age FROM Patient GROUP BY COALESCE(NULLIF(SEX, ''), 'Unknown');
SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT SEX) FROM Patient)
FROM Laboratory L
JOIN Patient P ON L.ID = P.ID;
SELECT P.SEX, CAST(COUNT(L.ID) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT P.ID) AS avg_records_per_patient
FROM Patient P
LEFT JOIN Laboratory L ON P.ID = L.ID
GROUP BY P.SEX
ORDER BY avg_records_per_patient DESC;
